title: AI Promises a Four-Day Workweek, but Employees Work 90 Hours of Overtime per Week: Tech Giants Themselves Haven't Achieved It

content_html:
Technology giants such as Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta invest billions of dollars annually in developing AI. For years, executives have painted the same future: when AI takes over more tasks, humans can work fewer days. OpenAI has even publicly called on companies to trial a four-day workweek without pay cuts, claiming AI will greatly increase labor efficiency. However, a BBC investigation found that these companies promoting shorter working hours have never lived up to their promises. Former OpenAI employees revealed that during their tenure, they worked at least 70 hours per week, and during peak periods, even over 90 hours, with weekends still being used to catch up or troubleshoot system failures.

Ironically, the more AI increases productivity, the longer employees' working hours become. Meta recently laid off about 10% of its staff while forcing many into AI project teams, which employees privately call "conscription"—refusing means resigning. After joining an AI team, working late into the night and continuing on weekends has become the norm, and even after work, they remain on standby. A former Google employee said that after the company continuously shifted processing power and storage resources to AI projects, internal engineering system failures became more frequent, often requiring them to stay up late to resolve issues. After leaving, their sleep and health conditions significantly improved.

The time saved by AI is consumed by new work

A study by the University of California, Berkeley, tracking hundreds of employees at a tech company for eight months revealed a core paradox: AI makes work faster and tasks broader, but the amount of time spent working each day actually gets longer. A key reason is that employees must constantly check whether AI-generated content is correct, a "supervision cost" that offsets the efficiency gains from AI. MIT innovation researchers pointed out that even if AI does save time, the saved portion will be swallowed by the work of system adjustments, implementation, and ensuring smooth operations.

A deeper driving force comes from employees' own anxiety. Some want to use the time saved to complete more work, while others fear that not continuously increasing output may prevent them from proving their value to employers. New work will always emerge, keeping the idea that "a 20% reduction in workload could lead to a four-day workweek" stuck in theory. Anthrop's CEO, Amodei, has openly stated that the higher the AI productivity, the more jobs may be eliminated in the future, further increasing employees' pressure to not relax. AI was supposed to do many things for humans, but in reality, at least in the core areas of the tech industry, more people are not sleeping better or living more easily, but instead falling into a cycle where the more efficient they are, the busier they become.

content_html_zh:
谷歌、OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 等科技巨头每年投资数十亿美元用于开发人工智能。 多年来，高管们描绘了同样的未来：当人工智能接管更多任务时，人类可以工作更少的天数。 OpenAI甚至公开呼吁企业在不减薪的情况下尝试每周工作四天，声称人工智能将大大提高劳动效率。 然而，BBC调查发现，这些提倡缩短工作时间的公司从未兑现过承诺。 前OpenAI员工透露，在他们任职期间，他们每周至少工作70个小时，高峰期甚至超过90个小时，周末仍然用来赶工或排除系统故障。

讽刺的是，人工智能提高生产力的程度越高，员工的工作时间就越长。 Meta 最近解雇了大约 10% 的员工，同时迫使许多人加入人工智能项目团队，员工私下称之为“征兵”——拒绝就意味着辞职。 加入AI团队后，加班到深夜、周末继续工作已经成为常态，甚至下班后也保持待命状态。 一位谷歌前员工表示，公司不断将处理能力和存储资源转移到AI项目后，内部工程系统故障变得更加频繁，常常需要他们熬夜解决问题。 离开后，他们的睡眠和健康状况明显改善。

人工智能节省的时间被新工作消耗掉了

加州大学伯克利分校的一项研究对一家科技公司的数百名员工进行了长达八个月的跟踪，揭示了一个核心悖论：人工智能使工作速度更快、任务更广泛，但每天工作的时间实际上却变得更长。 一个关键原因是员工必须不断检查人工智能生成的内容是否正确，这是抵消人工智能带来的效率收益的“监督成本”。 麻省理工学院创新研究人员指出，即使人工智能确实节省了时间，节省下来的部分也会被系统调整、实施和确保平稳运行的工作所吞噬。

更深层次的驱动力来自于员工自身的焦虑。 有些人希望利用节省下来的时间完成更多工作，而另一些人则担心，不持续增加产出可能会妨碍他们向雇主证明自己的价值。 新的工作总会出现，让“工作量减少 20% 就可以实现每周工作四天”的想法停留在理论上。 Anthrop首席执行官Amodei曾公开表示，AI生产力越高，未来可能被淘汰的工作岗位就越多，进一步加大员工不放松的压力。 人工智能本应为人类做很多事情，但现实中，至少在科技行业的核心领域，更多的人并不是睡得更好、生活得更轻松，而是陷入了越高效越忙碌的怪圈。
